x.articleBody:
A checklist is an enumerated set of terms that must be checked. Vector embeddings return fuzzy neighbours; they cannot enumerate a fixed set and report which members fired. A knowledge graph can.

I wrote up the machinery that wraps a Terraphim checklist around an LLM call. Before the call, terraphim-grep expands a query through a role thesaurus: 'quality gate' matched eight concepts in 53 ms, in files containing none of the query words. A control query reports kg_hits: 0 and says so. After the call, terraphim-agent hook returns a machine-readable findings list instead of a silent rewrite, and learn/memory feeds corrections back into the synonym set.

Every command output in the post is real, and the 39-entry public subset of the graph is committed in the site repo so you can run the same commands.

Which checklist in your agent setup would you rather see enforced by an automaton than by a system-prompt promise?

https://terraphim.ai/posts/graph-embeddings-checklists/
thread: A checklist is an enumerated set of terms that must be checked. Nearest neighbours can't enumerate; a knowledge graph can. nterm is the checklist head, synonyms:: are the items, and the Aho-Corasick automaton reports which items fired.

Before the LLM call: terraphim-grep 'quality gate' with a role thesaurus expanded into eight concepts (accept, fail, escalate, pass, judge-verdicts...) and matched chunks in files containing neither 'quality' nor 'gate'. 53 ms, no embedding model.
The honest empty case matters too: the control query 'checklist' returned kg_hits: 0 with an explicit sufficiency explanation. A checklist that can't say 'not covered' isn't a checklist.
After the LLM call: terraphim-agent hook --hook-type pre-tool-use returns a findings list ({matched_term: npm install, suggested_replacement: bun install}). A check that audits, not a silent rewrite.
Honest caveat included in the post: terraphim-agent replace in this build reports changed:true while returning the input unchanged. The findings-based hook is the contract; verify outputs, not flags.

Every artefact is public: the site's repo carries .terraphim/ with the kg concepts, the rewrite checklist and the compiled 39-entry thesaurus. Commands and outputs: https://terraphim.ai/posts/graph-embeddings-checklists/
